summary: A whole chat conversation from data: a header (avatar, name, status), the messages as bubbles (yours on the end side in the primary colour, theirs on the start side, with day separators, sender names, avatars, times, read status, reactions and attachments), the thread anchored to the bottom so the latest message shows and a drag scrolls back, and a composer row (a field that asks the app for input, a send button). From 720 dp a conversation list can show beside it.

messages.doc: One object per message, oldest first: {"text", "me", "name", "lead", "time", "day", "status", "react", "reactCount", "attachment", "label"}, all but text optional. me: true puts it on the end side in the primary colour (yours), else on the start side on surfaceHigh (theirs). name: the sender's name above the bubble (give it on the first message of a run in a group). lead: a node (an Avatar of 32 dp) beside the bubble, given on the LAST message of a run of theirs (needs avatars: true). time: the small time inside the bubble. day: a separator label shown above this message ("Today", "Mon 3 Nov"). status: a short line under your bubble ("Read 09:42", "Delivered"). react: a Material Symbols icon name (favorite, thumb_up) shown in a pill under the bubble, reactCount the number beside it. attachment: any node shown in the bubble above the text (a file or link card). label replaces the bubble's spoken text

title.doc: The conversation's name in the header (a person, a group, "Support")

subtitle.doc: Under the title: "online", "3 members", "Replies in a few minutes". Omitted: the title alone

placeholder.doc: The composer field's hint, shown while draft is empty

draft.doc: Text shown in the composer field instead of the hint: the app's draft, usually a host text variable ("@draft") the app fills from its own keyboard. Omitted: the hint

avatars.doc: true (a group): theirs are indented by 40 dp and a message's lead is drawn in that space. false (two people): theirs start at the edge

replies.doc: Quick replies, short strings shown as outlined chips above the composer (a bot's suggestions). A tap sends hostNamedAction replyAction with the chip's index (0-based) as a float

replyAction.doc: The host action name the quick replies send

onCompose.doc: Run when the composer field is tapped. The format has no text input: the app opens its own keyboard or input sheet and puts the text back through draft. Omitted: hostNamedAction "compose"

onSend.doc: Run by the send button. Omitted: hostNamedAction "send"

typing.doc: A typing line after the last message ("Mei is typing"), with three dots in a bubble on their side. Omitted: none

conversations.doc: Optional, wide windows only: the conversation list shown at the start from listAt, one object per conversation {"title", "preview", "meta", "lead", "unread"}. A tap sets selected (the app reads it and serves that thread). Omitted: the thread alone at every width

selected.doc: The highlighted conversation, from 0 (the thread shown). Bind an exported resources variable to read the taps. Do not name it step

listAt.doc: Width in dp from which the conversation list shows beside the thread (with conversations)

listWidth.doc: The conversation list's width when shown

bubbleShare.doc: A bubble's widest, as a share of the thread's width

maxBubble.doc: A bubble's widest in dp, on wide windows

maxThread.doc: The thread's widest in dp: on a wider pane it is centred, so yours and theirs do not drift to the far edges

width.doc: The width it has, when it is not the whole window

lead.doc: Before the title in the header: an Avatar (40 dp) of the person, group or bot

headerEnd.doc: At the end of the header: IconButtons (call, video, more)

composerStart.doc: Before the composer field: an IconButton (attach, add)

pitfalls: Give messages as data, oldest first, and let it lay out: yours (me: true) on the end side in color, theirs on the start side on surfaceHigh, each bubble wrapping at bubbleShare of the thread (0.78) and at most maxBubble (520 dp); from listAt (720 dp) with conversations the chat list takes listWidth (320 dp) at the start; the thread is centred at most maxThread (920 dp) wide. Decided by the window width, never by content

The thread is anchored to the bottom: the latest message sits right above the composer, a short thread sits at the bottom with empty space above (as in every messenger), and a drag down scrolls back to the oldest. The scroll is the component's own (a touchExpression and a translation by the measured thread height), not verticalScroll, whose position always starts at the top

Render or record with a few frames (render_rc duration 0.5, or any touch): the C++ player computes the thread's height-based translation from the previous layout, so a single-frame C++ render shows the thread pushed out of view. The TypeScript player and a running C++ player are right from the second frame

Nothing inside the thread is tappable: the bubbles are moved at paint time, so a click target in an attachment would not be under the finger. Put actions in the header (headerEnd), before the field (composerStart) or in replies

There is no text input in RemoteCompose: the field is a tap target that runs onCompose (default hostNamedAction compose) so the app can open its own keyboard, and shows draft (a host text variable, "@draft") or the placeholder. The send button runs onSend (default hostNamedAction send). The app appends the sent message and serves the new document

Group chats: avatars: true indents theirs by 40 dp; give name on the FIRST message of a run of one sender and lead (an Avatar of size 32) on the LAST, as messengers do. Without avatars, lead is ignored

attachment is any node, drawn full bubble width above the text (a file or invoice card on @colors.surface); the bubble then takes its widest. react is a Material Symbols name (favorite, thumb_up) in a pill under the bubble, reactCount the number; status is the muted line under it (Read 09:42, Seen by ...)

replies are chips in a horizontally scrolling row above the composer; every chip sends the same hostNamedAction (replyAction, default reply) with its index, so json2rc and the Java parser write different bytes (json2rc declares the shared name once on purpose): record it as meta.java_difference

selected is the highlighted conversation (0-based, only with conversations): bind an exported resources variable ("@chat") to read taps; the document holds one thread, the app serves the chosen one. Do not name a variable step
Text never cuts: bubbles wrap, titles and the field ellipsize on one line. Keep time and status short; a long subtitle ("Assistant, a person replies within 2 hours") ellipsizes on a phone
